item.title: Clenchwarton man sentenced for e-bike theft and drug-driving
item.description:
📰 FENLAND ANGELS RADIO | LOCAL NEWS
Clenchwarton man sentenced for e-bike theft and drug-driving
A 32-year-old man from Clenchwarton has been sentenced after admitting to theft and drug-driving offences at Lynn Magistrates’ Court. Shane Wilson was found in possession of a stolen £700 e-bike in Norwich this July, which had been tracked by its owner.
In a separate incident on April 4, Wilson was stopped by police while riding a motorbike at 45mph in a 30mph zone. Subsequent tests revealed he was over the legal limit for both cocaine and cannabis. Wilson has been handed an 18-month community order, including 40 hours of unpaid work and a mental health requirement. He is also banned from driving for 32 months and must pay a £114 victim surcharge.

item.description:
📰 FENLAND ANGELS RADIO | LOCAL NEWS
King’s Lynn Business Improvement District secures five-year extension
Businesses in King’s Lynn have voted to continue the Discover King’s Lynn initiative for another five years. Following a ballot of town centre traders, 75 percent of those who voted supported the renewal of the Business Improvement District. The organisation, which was first established in 2017, aims to attract visitors and support the local economy through events and various campaigns.
BID chairperson Sharon Edwards thanked the team and local partners, including the borough council and Norfolk Police, for their ongoing cooperation. The group now plans to implement its next five-year business strategy to further develop the town centre as a place to work and visit.

Gaywood man’s football magazine shortlisted for national award
A West Ham United fanzine edited by a Gaywood resident has been shortlisted for a national honour. The publication, which launched in 2012, has now produced 173 editions, offering fans a platform to share their views on the club.

item.description:
📰 FENLAND ANGELS RADIO | LOCAL NEWS
South Lynn man sentenced following nightclub incident
A 31-year-old man from South Lynn has been sentenced after being removed from a King’s Lynn nightclub. Arturas Cimolonskas of Fisheries Walk was ejected from Bar 100 on Norfolk Street during the early hours of Sunday, October 17, following reports of aggressive behaviour and intoxication.
Police issued a dispersal notice, but Mr Cimolonskas was subsequently arrested for being drunk and disorderly after failing to provide his details. Appearing at Lynn Magistrates’ Court on Thursday, he admitted the offence, claiming he only wished to re-enter the venue to retrieve a bag. Magistrates handed him a six-month conditional discharge and ordered him to pay £71 in costs and surcharges.

item.description:

West Norfolk Council reveals major parking and regeneration strategy for King’s Lynn
West Norfolk Council has unveiled a new strategy that could see several car parks in King’s Lynn replaced by housing, businesses, and public spaces. Under the proposals, the Tuesday Market Place would see its parking capacity reduced from 210 to 25 spaces to create a pedestrian-focused area. To compensate, the council is considering a new 517-space facility at the town’s port.
The plan aims to consolidate smaller car parks into larger, more efficient sites to support town centre regeneration. Officials have stated that the strategy is designed to maintain overall parking capacity rather than reduce it. The council is now moving forward with a £50,000 feasibility study before presenting final recommendations to the Cabinet.

item.title: Norfolk County Council confirms David Walliams books to remain in libraries
item.description:
📰 FENLAND ANGELS RADIO | LOCAL NEWS
Norfolk County Council confirms David Walliams books to remain in libraries
Norfolk County Council has announced that books by author David Walliams will stay on library shelves across the county. Despite recent allegations of misconduct against the comedian, the council confirmed that titles including Gangsta Granny and Mr Stink remain available for loan.
Councillor Pat Gould stated that the library service follows established ethical principles, noting that books are generally kept unless there is a legal reason for their removal. The council added that all library collections undergo regular reviews to ensure they meet the needs of residents while maintaining a diverse range of resources.
